## Decomposition design calls (2026-08-12, epic driver) — derived from the recorded direction, NOT new scope

Three placement questions the description leaves to implementation. Recording them here so the
children inherit one answer and reviewers can challenge it in one place.

**D1 — Storage home: a `.bridge_state` sidecar, NOT ticket `compiled_state`.**
New module `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/peer_confirmations.py`, store at
`.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/peer_confirmations.json`, modelled on `impossible_links.py`
(SCHEMA_VERSION, `record_key(source, target, relation)`, atomic mkstemp+os.replace save).
Rationale: the record carries the **Jira linkId** and is peer-derived, while
`src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py` is deliberately provider-agnostic (LOCAL ids only, so the
primitive is reusable for Linear/GitHub) — putting vendor link ids into reducer state would
break that and would emit a ticket event (auto-committed + auto-pushed to the `tickets` branch)
on every outbound link push. All other peer-derived state already lives in `.bridge_state`
(bindings.json peer baselines, `peer_parent` via `peer_state.py`).
The description's "survives SNAPSHOT compaction" constraint is satisfied **trivially** by a
sidecar (ticket-log compaction cannot touch it) and S1 asserts it with a behavioral test rather
than inheriting it. **Load-bearing consequence:** the new file MUST be added to the staged
`_rel_files` list in `reconcile_helpers.py::_commit_binding_store_snapshot` or it is lost on
every CI checkout — this is bug b8b1's recorded lesson.

**D2 — Key shape: `(source_local_id, target_local_id, relation)`, relation-scoped.**
Matches the consumer (`_inbound_unlink_one`, relation-scoped since e39f) and the existing
`impossible_links.record_key`. Deliberately NOT the outbound ADD dedup key
`(vendor_type, target_key)`, which is direction-agnostic and explicitly not relation-keyed
(`outbound_links.py::_diff_links` docstring) — that key cannot express the granularity G3 needs.
No translation cost: the outbound ADD payload already carries `relation`, so the dispatch
success point has it in hand.

**D3 — "confirming snapshot revision" == `pass_id`.**
The codebase has no snapshot revision counter, ETag, or monotonic remote version; `pass_id` is
the only handle identifying which fetch confirmed a link. Records therefore store
`confirmed_pass` (the pass id) + `confirmed_at` (epoch ns) rather than an ordered revision.
Ordering-sensitive logic must not be built on it.

Write point for outbound confirmation: `dispatch_one.py::_update_one_dispatch_links`, immediately
after `set_relationship` succeeds (the sole `set_relationship` call site in the engine).
Snapshot-confirmation seam: the persist phase of `reconcile.py`, as a sibling of the existing
`_advance_baselines(binding_store, ctx.curr_snapshot, ...)` call — the established precedent for
"learn peer state from the current snapshot at end of pass".
Completeness signal for S2 already exists and needs no new mechanism:
`fetcher.py::merge_issuelinks_map` writes the `issuelinks` key ONLY on an authoritative read
(absent key == unobserved; `[]` == authoritative-empty), and `BackendPaginationStallError`
re-raises rather than degrading.
